# Top 15 merchants by total spend

Files: `top_merchants.pdf`, `top_merchants.svg` (this file: `top_merchants.md`), written by `ob_figures.py` (task T25).

**The data are synthetic.** They were generated by `ob_generator.py` from ONS averages (Family Spending, uprated), FCA Financial Lives 2024 holding rates and stated synthetic assumptions, so this figure describes the generator, not real customers.

## Source data

Source: the 100 files `Analysis/open_banking/persona*.json` (Open Banking Read/Write v3.1 objects; seed 20261107) and `Analysis/open_banking/ground_truth.csv`, written by `ob_generator.py` at commit `4287a78`; read by `ob_figures.py` (commit `unknown` or later). Plot style: `TeXFormat.py` sha256 `a33ce9f67e0a`. No random numbers are drawn here (seed: not applicable).

## Filters, transformations and units

All booked card purchases (everyday and one-off, defined below) at each `MerchantName`, summed over all 100 persons and
12 months. **Everyday spending** = booked card purchases (proprietary codes `DEB` debit card and `PUR` credit card, which carry `MerchantDetails`) from every account of a person, excluding own-account transfers (any transaction whose `TransactionReference` also appears on another transaction of the same person) and; here one-off purchases are **included** and shown as the
red part of each bar. The 15 merchants with the largest total are plotted (of 68 merchants in all). Amounts in GBP.
Plotted data and all merchants: [`Analysis/open_banking_figures/merchants.csv`](../../Analysis/open_banking_figures/merchants.csv).

## Statistics

Totals only; no error bars, tests or fits (not applicable). The top 15 account for 56.1% of all card spending.

## Interpretation

JET2HOLIDAYS has the largest total (GBP 73,020.54), driven by one-off purchases where the red segment is large
(73,020.54 GBP). Among everyday merchants, the supermarkets lead. The merchant list and the share of each
merchant within a category are assumptions of the generator, not market shares.
